summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the fourth condition of salah: proper covering of the awrah (the parts of the body that must be covered during prayer). He explains the etymological meaning of awrah and establishes that Islamic scholars unanimously agree on the requirement to cover the awrah during salah, based on Quranic evidence from Surah Al-A'raf verse 31. Sh. Ali Mashhour provides historical context by explaining the pre-Islamic practice of making tawaf (circumambulation) around the Kaaba naked, which was promoted by the Quraysh tribes as a business strategy and claimed superiority over pilgrims from outside Mecca. He details how this innovation, called 'Ahdas,' created a caste system where only clothing purchased from Mecca or borrowed from Quraysh was considered acceptable. Allah revealed this verse to refute this practice and establish clear guidelines for modesty during worship.
